answer: Hypothesis: The Diversity in Pottery Form collapsed and the Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased simultaneously in the 17th century BCE (approximately 1700 BCE). In the raw 100-year-binned Z-score record (4100–500 BCE), Pottery Form drops sharply from +0.74 (at 1800 BCE) to −1.13 — its series minimum (at 1700 BCE) — while Pottery Decoration rises from −0.48 to +0.97 in that same step. This is the only bin in the entire series where Pottery Form declines and Pottery Decoration increases together. The transition is registered between the 1800 and 1700 BCE bins, and the collapsed-Form / elevated-Decoration state is first observed at the 1700 BCE data point; under the strict/historical convention (17th century BCE = 1700–1601 BCE) this places the event in the 17th century BCE. Context: the step occurs within the Late Neolithic.

payload.workflow: Used the raw 100-year bins of PotteryForm and PotteryDecoration from time_series_data.csv (37 points, 4100-500 BCE), which match capital.csv ZKeform/Zkeverz exactly (37/37). Computed per-bin deltas (Form[t]-Form[t-1], Dec[t]-Dec[t-1]) and flagged bins where Form decreases and Decoration increase simultaneously; the 1700 BCE bin is the unique maximum (dForm=-1.87, dDec=+1.45). Cross-checked with the annual linearly-interpolated columns (_inter), which localize the transition to the 1800->1700 BCE interval. Mapped the winning bin to a century with the strict/historical rule century=ceil(year_BCE/100). Context: Late Neolithic.
